item.title: Elections Coordinator
item.description: Allegan County has much to offer, with 24 Townships, 9 Cities, and 2 Villages across nearly 900 square miles. The landscapes range from the lakeshore to beautifully wooded lands, our County’s natural resources are a gift to be treasured. Allegan County businesses, citizens, and employees are world-class, and we remain a welcoming, closely-knit community. We are one of the fastest-growing counties in Michigan. Allegan County Government places high importance on our core values: Respect, Integrity, Commitment and Honesty. A common thread among our leadership, employees and volunteers is a strong desire to serve and be part of something meaningful. We have been recognized by Gallagher as “Best in Class Winner” among mid-size companies for our excellence in optimizing employee and organizational well-being for three years in a row (2023-2025). We have also received the “Impact Award” from M.E.R.S. for excellence in educating our employees about their retirement plans and overall financial wellness. We are looking for dedicated, caring, energetic people to join our team! Summary: Coordinates and manages election activities and election reporting within the county. Coordinates voter registration and election activities between the municipal clerks, the Bureau of Elections and the Secretary of State Office. Starting Wage: $28.54/hr , Full-Time, Benefit Eligible Excellent Benefits Plan: Health insurance begins on the first of the month after your hire date - Medical, Dental & Vision (3 medical plans to choose from, 2 of which have a $0 biweekly premium) - County-funded Health Savings Account with our two high-deductible medical plans - County-paid employee life insurance coverage - County-paid short-term disability coverage, up to 52 weeks - Generous retirement plan, including a county contribution of 7% of your annual earnings - Tuition Reimbursement Program for college degree courses - Generous PTO plan, including front-loaded hours into PTO bank at hire, and annually on January 1. - 13 paid holidays, in addition to PTO - FREE use of Allegan County government's two fitness centers Essential Duties: Receives voter registration applications from various sources. Prepares reports to the State and monitors reimbursements. Develops and updates all contracts and coordinating agreements while serving as school districts election coordinator for all schools within the Allegan Area Educational Service Agency. Assists candidates and treasurers of campaign committees with compliance and disclosure requirements of the Michigan Campaign Finance Act. Accepts candidate filings for State Office, County Office, and School Board and reviews for compliance. Maintains logs for petitions and/or filing fees for review after the primary and maintains all election results. Maintains the State Qualified Voter file and the county voter registration data base for each election. Schedules meetings of the Election Commission and takes minutes. Monitors the deadlines on the election schedule to ensure meetings are held according to the requirements for each election. Determines what format is required for reporting and canvassing forms for the permanent record and prepares the reports to comply with the requirements. Monitors the filing of Acceptance of Office forms for school board candidates. Verifies correct programming and operation of voting system equipment and provides training as needed on equipment. Communicates both verbally and written to various entities requesting elections information, this includes media outlets, and in-training of election workers. Required Education and Experience: High School Diploma or equivalent GED. Ability to obtain certification and training required by Secretary of State, Bureau of Elections. Two (2) years of experience working for an election support company. Possession of a valid Michigan driver’s license . Preferred Education and Experience: One (1) year of experience with local clerk’s office. Associate’s Degree in technology or closely related field. *Candidates must pass a drug screen (which includes testing for THC) in order to be hired for this position.

item.title: Senior Account Supervisor Public Government Affairs
item.description: We are in relentless pursuit of an equitable and inspiring workplace that is respectful of all, reflects and represents the world in which we live, and fosters trust, collaboration and belonging. Consistent with this approach, we hire the best qualified candidates for all positions. About the Role Edelman’s Public & Government Affairs team helps clients navigate complex policy, political, regulatory, reputational, and stakeholder environments. We bring together communications strategy, public affairs expertise, media relations, research, digital strategy, stakeholder engagement, and campaign execution to help organizations build trust, shape conversations, and advance business and policy priorities. Our team is seeking a Senior Account Supervisor to support integrated public affairs, policy communications, and stakeholder engagement programs for clients operating at the intersection of business, government, and public policy. This role is ideal for a strong communications professional with experience translating complex policy issues into clear, compelling strategies and content for policymaker, stakeholder, media, and public audiences. The successful candidate will bring hands-on experience in policy communications, preferably gained through work in government, on Capitol Hill, at a trade association, within a public affairs agency, or in a corporate public affairs environment. Experience with energy policy is strongly preferred. The Senior Account Supervisor will serve as a day-to-day client counselor, project manager, and communications strategist, helping develop and execute programs that advance client priorities in a dynamic policy and media environment. Key Responsibilities Policy Communications and Public Affairs Strategy Develop and execute public affairs and policy communications strategies that support client business, reputational, and advocacy objectives. Translate complex legislative, regulatory, and policy issues into clear, persuasive messaging for diverse audiences, including policymakers, stakeholders, media, employees, and the public. Monitor and analyze policy, political, regulatory, and media developments relevant to client priorities, with a focus on energy, infrastructure, sustainability, innovation, and related public policy issues. Support the development of integrated communications plans that connect policy goals with earned media, stakeholder engagement, thought leadership, digital, and advocacy tactics. Client Management Serve as a primary day-to-day contact for clients, helping manage workstreams, deadlines, deliverables, and expectations. Provide thoughtful counsel to clients and internal teams on public affairs strategy, message development, stakeholder dynamics, and policy communications opportunities. Prepare client-ready materials, including messaging documents, talking points, policy one-pagers, memos, briefing materials, media materials, campaign plans, and executive communications. Help ensure client work is delivered on time, on strategy, and at a high standard of quality. Energy Policy and Issue Expertise Bring knowledge of, or strong interest in energy policy issues, including areas such as energy production, transmission, grid reliability, clean energy, permitting, infrastructure, manufacturing, climate, sustainability, and federal or state energy policy debates. Help clients navigate the communications implications of energy policy, regulatory developments, legislative activity, and stakeholder scrutiny. Identify opportunities for clients to engage constructively in policy conversations through thought leadership, stakeholder engagement, earned media, coalitions, and advocacy campaigns. Have an understanding of the earned media landscape, and have the experience of pitching media. Campaign and Digital Execution Support the planning and execution of public affairs campaigns, including advocacy, reputation, stakeholder, and issue-based campaigns. Work with digital, creative, paid media, research, and earned media specialists to develop integrated campaign tactics. Help develop content for campaign channels, including social media, websites, email, toolkits, paid media, and stakeholder outreach. Experience with political campaigns, grassroots or grasstops advocacy, coalition campaigns, or digital campaign development is a plus. Writing, Research, and Content Development Draft high-quality written materials for clients and internal teams, including strategic plans, policy memos, op-eds, press materials, stakeholder letters, social content, executive briefing documents, and presentation materials. Conduct research and analysis to support client recommendations, new business opportunities, policy positioning, and campaign strategy. Synthesize complicated information quickly and produce clear, accurate, and actionable communications materials. Team Collaboration and Project Management Manage multiple client workstreams simultaneously while coordinating across internal teams and specialty functions. Help guide junior team members by providing direction, edits, feedback, and support on client deliverables. Collaborate with colleagues across Edelman, including public affairs, corporate reputation, crisis, digital, creative, research, paid media, and sector experts. Support project management, staffing coordination, budget tracking, and internal communications to ensure smooth account operations. New Business and Organic Growth Contribute to new business and organic growth efforts by supporting research, strategy development, proposal writing, and pitch preparation. Identify opportunities to expand client work based on emerging policy issues, reputational needs, campaign opportunities, or stakeholder dynamics. Bring an entrepreneurial mindset and a strong interest in helping grow Edelman’s Public & Government Affairs offering. Basic Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in communications, public relations, political science, public policy, journalism, government affairs, or a related field. 5+ years of relevant experience in public affairs, policy communications, government affairs, political campaigns, Capitol Hill, a trade association, corporate communications, or an agency environment. Preferred Qualifications Experience working on or around energy policy or in communications around energy, including energy production, clean energy, utilities, transmission, permitting, infrastructure, sustainability, or related policy issues. Demonstrated experience developing communications materials related to public policy, legislative, regulatory, or political issues. Prior experience in government, on Capitol Hill, at a trade association, in a political campaign, or in a public affairs agency. Experience supporting advocacy, coalition, issue, or reputation campaigns. Familiarity with digital campaign development, social media strategy, paid media, or grassroots/grasstops engagement. Strong understanding of Washington, D.C. policy, media, and stakeholder dynamics. Ability to make complex policy issues understandable and relevant to business, public, and policymaker audiences. Strong client service orientation, attention to detail, and ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced environment. Interest in mentoring junior colleagues and contributing to a positive, high-performing team culture. Core Competencies Excellent writer and communicator. Strong policy and political judgment. Client-ready presence and professional maturity. Ability to connect policy developments to communications strategy. Strong project management and organizational skills. Collaborative, proactive, and solutions-oriented. Comfortable working across disciplines and with senior internal and client stakeholders. Curious, adaptable, and eager to build expertise in complex public policy issues. $80,000 - $120,000 a year #LI-JLF An employee’s pay position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, travel requirements, revenue-based metrics, any contractual agreements, and business or organizational needs. The range listed is just one component of DJEH’s total compensation package for employees. Other rewards may include annual bonuses, a Paid Time Off policy, and region-specific benefits. DJEH offers a wide range of benefits: medical and dental insurance, vision, 401K, life insurance, disability insurance, paid time off, travel assistance and wellness programing. DJEH is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and believes in diversity, equity, and inclusion. We seek applications from all qualified candidates without regard to race, color, gender, sex, age, religion, physical or mental disability, military and veteran status, or any other basis protected by federal, state or local law. If you require a reasonable accommodation in any part of the employment process, please let us know.

item.title: Poll Worker Program Coordinator San Francisco Department Of Elections 1404 Clerk
item.description: Department Background The mission of the Department of Elections (Department) is to provide equitable access to voting and election-related services and to conduct free, fair, and functional elections for the City and County of San Francisco. Department staff work year-round to ensure that every eligible San Franciscan has easy access to safe, barrier-free registration and voting options. The Department also works continuously to improve its elections programs with the goal of making them ever more efficient and responsive to the needs of San Francisco voters. The Department strives to cultivate a workplace environment in which employees of all racial and ethnic backgrounds feel respected, valued, and supported in providing the fairest and most effective services possible to San Francisco residents. The Department is committed to maintaining an inclusive workplace and to providing the training and resources necessary for all employees to succeed in delivering equitable services to city residents. The Department is committed to reaching job seekers of all backgrounds. Everyone, including job seekers from underrepresented communities, is strongly encouraged to apply. Position Description In preparation for the November 3, 2026, General Election, the Department is seeking applications for seasonal positions of Poll Worker Program Coordinator. Beginning a few months before each election, Poll Worker Program Coordinators work to recruit, train, assign, and support paid volunteers who will serve as poll workers on Election Day. As part of this process, Coordinators play a key role in ensuring 501 polling places are fully staffed, poll workers are properly trained and supported, and Election Day operations run smoothly and effectively. In addition to the range of duties assigned to the 1404 job code, https://careers.sf.gov/classifications/?classCode=1404&setId=COMMN , the persons in these positions will have the following essential duties and responsibilities: Coordinate the recruitment, onboarding, training, assignment, and support of poll worker in preparation for Election Day. Maintain regular communication with poll workers via mail, email and phone. Utilize the Department’s Election Information Management System (EIMS) to process poll worker applications enroll poll workers in training classes, update records, and track poll worker progress. Maintain Excel spreadsheets and tracking tools to organize poll worker assignments, ensuring all Election Day sites are fully staffed. Process incoming and outgoing mail including opening, sorting, and preparing election-related correspondence. Demonstrate strong communication skills when speaking with volunteers or other members of the public. Driving to and assisting with offsite outreach and poll worker recruitment events. Conduct and assist with poll worker trainings. Assist in the Election Center providing remote support to poll workers on Election Day. Assisting with post-election tasks as needed. Position Schedule, Requirements, and Work Location These are seasonal positions with a tentative start date of September 1, 2026. The tentative end date for these positions is approximately November 22, 2026. Actual start and end dates will depend upon the Department’s operational needs. Work will primarily be on site at the Department of Elections Office at City Hall, San Francisco, CA. Travel within the city and field work will be required as needed. Work hours will vary in accordance with the demands of the election cycle and will range between 20 and 40 hours per week. Although most work is expected to be completed during normal workday hours, 8 a.m.-5 p.m., Monday through Friday, employees must be available to work overtime both during the week and on weekends as necessary. Overtime hours will be paid at 1.5 the hourly rate. This is a temporary exempt as-needed position. Temporary exempt as-needed employees who have worked more than 1040 hours in any consecutive 12-month period, and whose normal work week at the time of inclusion in the system is not less than 20 hours are eligible for health coverage and retirement benefits. For more information on the City and County of San Francisco benefit policies, refer to the Department of Human Resources website at https://careers.sf.gov/benefits/ . Position Salary: $32.1625 to $39.10 hourly $66,898 to $81,328 annually Minimum Qualifications: One (1) year of clerical experience including preparing and maintaining a variety of records and/or documents, filing, use of office equipment, public contact and processing of incoming and outgoing mail. Substitution: Completion of an approved City and County of San Francisco Clerical Administrative Training program, or completion of a clerical training program (240 hours), or 15 semester units (or equivalent quarter units) of coursework from an accredited college or university may substitute for up to 6 months of required experience. Desirable Qualifications: The ideal candidate will: Have demonstrated ability to quickly learn new systems, procedures, and election-related subject matter in a deadline-driven environment Have experience with public-facing roles such as outreach, training facilitation, or customer service. Possess a high level of computer literacy, particularly proficiency with Excel, Outlook, and databases Be meticulously organized and able to maintain enthusiasm, patience, and a positive demeanor Have a strong team work ethic and can-do/will-do attitude, and solid interpersonal and conflict resolution skills Have the willingness and flexibility to work extended hours, evenings, weekends, and overtime as required during the election cycle. Possess a basic understanding of San Francisco geography and neighborhood location/demography Demonstrate a commitment to excellent public service and impartiality How to Apply: In addition to the standard City and County employment application, applicants must submit a resume and a cover letter in order to be considered. Resumes will not be accepted in lieu of a completed City and County of San Francisco application. Additional Requirement: This position requires a valid California driver’s license and a clean DMV record. Successful candidates will be required to show their valid CA driver’s license and provide a copy of their latest DMV record before an offer can be made. To be considered for the position, applications must be submitted by 5 p.m. July 31, 2026. If you have any questions regarding this recruitment or application process, please contact the Elections Hiring Team at [email protected] . Additional Information Regarding Employment with the City and County of San Francisco: Carol Isen - Human Resources Director All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. The City and County of San Francisco encourages women, minorities and persons with disabilities to apply. Applicants will be considered regardless of their sex, race, age, religion, color, national origin, ancestry, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition (associated with cancer, a history of cancer, or genetic characteristics), HIV/AIDS status, genetic information, marital status, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, military and veteran status, or other protected category under the law.

item.title: Applied Scientist Amazon Selection And Catalog Systems Ascs
item.description: At Amazon Selection and Catalog Systems (ASCS), our mission is to power the online buying experience for customers worldwide so they can find, discover, and buy any product they want. We innovate on behalf of our customers to infer relationships between products in Amazon Catalog to drive the selection gateway for the search and browse experiences on the website. We're solving a fundamental AI challenge: establishing product identity and relationships at unprecedented scale. Using Generative AI, Visual Language Models (VLMs), and multimodal reasoning, we determine what makes each product unique and how products relate to one another across Amazon's catalog. The scale is staggering: billions of products, petabytes of multimodal data, millions of sellers, dozens of languages, and infinite product diversity—from electronics to groceries to digital content. The research challenges are immense. GenAI and VLMs hold transformative promise for catalog understanding, but we operate where traditional methods fail: ambiguous problem spaces, incomplete and noisy data, inherent uncertainty, reasoning across both images and textual data, and explaining decisions at scale. Establishing product identities and groupings requires sophisticated models that reason across text, images, and structured data—while maintaining accuracy and trust for high-stakes business decisions affecting millions of customers daily. Amazon's Item and Relationship Platform group is looking for an innovative and customer-focused applied scientist to help us make the world's best product catalog even better. In this role, you will partner with technology and business leaders to build new state-of-the-art algorithms, models, and services to infer product-to-product relationships that matter to our customers. You will pioneer advanced GenAI solutions that power next-generation agentic shopping experiences, working in a collaborative environment where you can experiment with massive data from the world's largest product catalog, tackle problems at the frontier of AI research, rapidly implement and deploy your algorithmic ideas at scale, across millions of customers. Key job responsibilities * Formulate novel research problems at the intersection of GenAI, multimodal learning, and large-scale information retrieval—translating ambiguous business challenges into tractable scientific frameworks * Design and implement leading models leveraging VLMs, foundation models, and agentic architectures to solve product identity, relationship inference, and catalog understanding at billion-product scale * Pioneer explainable AI methodologies that balance model performance with scalability requirements for production systems impacting millions of daily customer decisions * Own end-to-end ML pipelines from research ideation to production deployment—processing petabytes of multimodal data with rigorous evaluation frameworks * Define research roadmaps aligned with business priorities, balancing foundational research with incremental product improvements * Mentor peer scientists and engineers on advanced ML techniques, experimental design, and scientific rigor—building organizational capability in GenAI and multimodal AI * Represent the team in the broader science community—publishing findings, delivering tech talks, and staying at the forefront of GenAI, VLM, and agentic system research - PhD, or Master's degree and 4+ years of CS, CE, ML or related field experience - Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language - PhD - 2+ years of CS, CE, ML or related field experience - Have publications at top-tier peer-reviewed conferences or journals - Proven track record of successfully applying ML-based solutions to complex problems in business, science, or engineering. Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner.

item.title: Senior Principal Site Selection Manager
item.description: Description This role will be responsible for performing global analytics and conducting market research in targeted metros and regions, developing site selection opportunities, determining market rates, negotiating commercial terms with data center operators and stakeholders, and constructing and negotiating complex lease agreements and associated legal documents. This will include Master Service Agreements, NRC service orders, new lease agreements, lease renewals, operating agreements and amendments. Site Selection manager is responsible to negotiate strong commercial terms, align base build and data hall design to Oracle’s desired specs and drive accountability with data center operators to ensure on-time delivery and operational compliance. Role requires strengths in stakeholder management, analytics, negotiation, and a drive to execute. Responsibilities Qualifications: Strong experience in leading complex negotiations, contract formation, and contract negotiations on Data Center contracts. Experience in site selection for industrial-scale projects, real estate evaluation, acquisition, development, construction, lease agreements, infrastructure delivery, and general awareness of utility agreements, sustainable practices, and financial modeling. Excellent stakeholder management skills and an ability to obtain engineering experts’ feedback to drive contract negotiation and technical due diligence. Knowledge of the Data Center industry, operators in region and market dynamics Strong collaborator, working closely with multiple teams and subject matter experts, driving and resolving questions effectively. Knowledge of real estate and mission critical environments, such as Data Centers A general background in real estate development and land acquisition is a plus – with an understanding of local laws, permitting, etc. Confident, takes ownership, willingness to do what it takes” to get the job done with proven experience leading complex negotiations/initiatives to successful completion. Understanding of hybrid real estate solutions such as Build-to-suit, Retail, and Wholesale leases Leading contributor individually and as a team member, and ability to progress workstreams independently, but seeking direction from others as needed. Excellent problem solver with the ability to operate in fast pace, ambiguous environment. Work is non-routine and very complex, involving the application of advanced technical/business skills in area of specialization. Strong capabilities in excel with a desire to analyze and manage global data and capacity opportunities. 5+ years relevant experience and BA/BS degree. Positive Attitude: Ability to contribute consistently and positively in a high-paced, fast-changing and at time unpredictable work environment. Ability to be a strong team player, plus an ability to deliver independently; must be able to deliver results or projects in a timely manner within project metrics. Strong analytical, creative thinking, written, and verbal communications skills. Willing to travel globally to conduct data center visits (50%) Responsibilities: Be accountable for lease execution from demand signal through to ‘general availability’ date – driving each performance metric (safety, quality, rates, schedule, cost, etc.) within critical timelines required by the business. Manage multiple lease projects and coordinate with internal team members, consultants, vendors, and external stakeholders. Work with capacity (demand) planners and network specialists to understand capacity needs and site requirements in assigned metros/regions. Lead cross-functional teams to evaluate, select, negotiate, and recommend leases for approval. Develop high-quality metro strategies based on market expertise, within the context of time-to-market and cost efficiencies required by the business units. Drive commercial terms with our lease providers in the region. Work with internal Corporate Procurement personnel to drive executable lease documents. Work with Finance team to conduct Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) lease or build options to recommend the most favorable strategies for assigned metros. Qualifications Disclaimer: Certain U.S. based or U.S. customer or client-facing roles may be required to comply with applicable requirements, such as immunization/occupational health mandates, and/or drug testing requirements. item.title: Lead Principal Strategic Data Center Site Selection
item.description: Description Oracle Cloud Infrastructure is seeking a highly experienced Lead Principal, Data Center & Power Sourcing to drive strategic, critical, and high-impact infrastructure programs directly supporting the EVP of Infrastructure. This is a highly visible senior individual contributor role at the center of Oracle’s data center growth strategy, focused on accelerating capacity, power, and site sourcing decisions that enable the business to meet rapidly evolving customer and product demand. This individual will work across executive leadership, capacity planning, data center engineering, power and utilities, networking, construction, finance, legal, security, compliance, procurement, and operations to shape and execute complex sourcing strategies. The role requires exceptional judgment, executive presence, analytical depth, and the ability to turn ambiguous, fast-moving inputs into crisp recommendations, decision-ready materials, and executable plans. The ideal candidate is a strategic operator who can move quickly, communicate clearly with senior executives, manage sensitive and high-stakes workstreams, and drive outcomes across multiple stakeholders without waiting for perfect information. Responsibilities Key Responsibilities Lead strategic data center and power sourcing initiatives that directly support the priorities of the EVP of Infrastructure. Drive high-priority programs requiring quick turnarounds, strong executive communication, and clear decision-making under ambiguity. Develop and present executive-ready materials, including investment write-ups, sourcing recommendations, market assessments, risk summaries, and decision memos. Evaluate global and regional data center and power opportunities, including site availability, market dynamics, utility readiness, commercial terms, delivery risk, cost, schedule, and scalability. Partner with capacity planning, engineering, construction, networking, finance, legal, procurement, security, compliance, and operations teams to align sourcing strategy with business demand. Lead cross-functional workstreams to evaluate, negotiate, and recommend data center, power, lease, build-to-suit, wholesale, retail, and hybrid infrastructure solutions. Conduct market research on targeted metros, countries, regions, data center providers, power markets, utility constraints, and emerging infrastructure opportunities. Support commercial negotiations with data center operators, landowners, utilities, developers, and other external stakeholders. Help structure and negotiate complex agreements, including leases, service orders, operating agreements, amendments, renewals, power-related agreements, and related commercial documents. Drive accountability across internal and external partners to ensure delivery against safety, quality, cost, schedule, capacity, operational, and business requirements. Build and maintain accurate systems of record, executive reporting, program dashboards, and materials that improve leadership visibility into sourcing priorities and risks. Identify risks, tradeoffs, dependencies, and decision points early, and proactively escalate with clear recommendations. Operate as a trusted strategic partner to the Chief of Staff, Head of Business Operations, and senior Infrastructure leadership on critical initiatives. Required Qualifications Significant experience leading complex data center, infrastructure, energy, power, site selection, real estate, procurement, development, or commercial sourcing initiatives. Strong understanding of data center markets, operators, site selection, lease structures, infrastructure delivery, and mission-critical environments. Experience with complex negotiations, contract formation, commercial terms, and cross-functional deal execution. Familiarity with power sourcing, utility engagement, grid constraints, sustainable infrastructure practices, and power-related commercial considerations. Exceptional executive communication skills, including the ability to synthesize complex information into clear, concise, decision-ready narratives. Proven ability to support senior executives on strategic, high-visibility, and time-sensitive priorities. Strong analytical skills, including market analysis, financial modeling, TCO analysis, scenario planning, and risk assessment. Excellent stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence across technical, commercial, legal, finance, and executive audiences. Demonstrated ability to operate independently in a fast-paced, ambiguous, and rapidly changing environment. Strong ownership mindset and willingness to do what it takes to drive critical workstreams to completion. Ability to manage multiple priorities, deliver high-quality work quickly, and maintain accuracy under pressure. Strong written and verbal communication skills. item.title: Election Administration And Field Associate
item.description: Job Title: Election Administration and Field Associate Organization: Michigan United Nature of Work: 501(c)(3) The Election Administration and Field Associate serves as the operational backbone of Michigan United’s election protection program. This role develops and maintains the vital infrastructure that makes our field deployments possible: building local clerk relationships, managing the challenger credentialing pipeline, building data models, and coordinating with our coalition partners. Because election administration requires continuous engagement, this is a year-round position. The relationships cultivated in the winter shape what Michigan United can achieve in August, and the frameworks built after the general election serve as the foundation for the following cycle. As the division’s primary liaison to Michigan’s election administration community, the Associate builds collaborative, professional relationships with local clerks to deeply understand each jurisdiction's unique dynamics. This ensures Michigan United operates with the highest level of professionalism and effectiveness when it matters most. This role is beautifully balanced between relationship-building and technical data management. You will serve as our internal expert on BOB (Michigan United’s internal field data system), VoteGuard (our coalition site-coverage platform), and the organization’s precinct analysis models. About Michigan United Michigan United is building a vibrant, inclusive democracy in Michigan where community members organize to build power to affect change at local, state, and national levels. We work to dismantle systemic barriers perpetuating inequality by building power. Michigan United defines power as the ability to act, which comes in the form of organized people and organized money. We focus on issues through a racial, economic, gender, immigrant, and environmental justice lens, serving as a hub of people-centered leadership development, issue organizing, and civic power building. We are guided by our Theory of Change. We are dedicated to dismantling oppressive systems and transforming lives through tangible victories and leadership development. We believe in the power of a united community driven by a shared vision and strategic action. Our commitment to a democracy that reflects our base is at the core of our work, guiding us as we organize and mobilize communities, build collective power, and seek just outcomes. We aim to create a Michigan where the government and our economy are inclusive, accountable, and equitable. Michigan United's approach is grounded in practicality, driven by our values, and focused on building a state where dignity, equity, and justice are realities, not just aspirations. Through strong relationship-building, continuous leadership development, and strategic collective action, we are paving the way for the systemic changes our communities deserve. We are a statewide organization of community members and institutions fighting for the dignity and potential of every person. Position Details and Responsibilities 1. Clerk Engagement and Election Administrator Relationships Cultivating long-term, trusted relationships with local election officials is a cornerstone of this role. Supporting targeted municipalities across Wayne, Genesee, Saginaw, Oakland, Washtenaw, and Macomb counties, the Associate maintains active, open communication with local election administrators. Relationship Tracking: Maintain a living engagement log for targeted municipalities, tracking key contact information, relationship status, ongoing conversations, and follow-up tasks. Log Maintenance: Keep the engagement log consistently updated following clerk interactions to ensure accurate organizational records. Goal Alignment: Ensure targeted municipal profiles are thoroughly mapped out and active ahead of the primary season, keeping leadership informed of progress during active election periods. Convenings & Spaces: Represent Michigan United at key administrator convenings, including the Michigan Department of State Democracy Partner Meeting and the Election Official Workgroup. Operational Insights: Build collaborative dynamics that provide early insights into site logistics, equipment changes, polling location alterations, and other adjustments impacting field planning. County Protocols: Coordinate Oakland County clerk engagement in alignment with the Oakland Forward protocol, ensuring collaboration frameworks are finalized prior to launching local program activities. 2. Credentialing Pipeline (Primary and General Elections) Michigan United directly manages its own challenger credentialing process. The Associate guides the entire pipeline, from initial application tracking through Election Day site assignments. Regulatory Compliance: Develop a deep understanding of the Michigan statutory credentialing framework, including application windows, site capacity limits, permissible challenge guidelines, and the differing protocols for early voting vs. Election Day and absent voter processing facilities. Application Submissions: Manage and submit primary election credentialing applications by the mid-May statutory deadline. General Election Scaling: Oversee general election credentialing applications with a goal of confirming 250 credentialed challengers by August. Data Organization: Maintain a clear credentialing tracker detailing challenger names, site assignments, training statuses, and contact logs. Capacity Mapping: Proactively connect with priority county clerks ahead of elections to confirm challenger capacity limits at absent voter processing facilities. Early Voting Strategy: Coordinate credentialing logistics for the early voting windows, aiming to support 30–40 primary sites and 60–75 general election sites. Pipeline Updates: Monitor site coverage closely and collaborate with the Deputy Director to quickly address any regional volunteer gaps. 3. Precinct Analysis and Scoring Model Our precinct data model guides our site prioritization, resource sharing, and volunteer deployment. The Associate maintains and refines this model to keep our strategies data-driven. Model Upkeep: Maintain the living precinct data model for target areas, integrating prior incident data, demographic trends, historical barriers to voting, and partner feedback. Strategic Validation: Review and update the data model with the Deputy Director ahead of primary and general early voting windows. Field Guidance: Use model outputs to provide data-backed recommendations for volunteer placements, high-priority site double-coverage, and Poll Chaplain locations. Post-Election Refinement: Integrate post-election feedback and field data back into the model within 30 days of an election to continually sharpen our approach. Coalition Sharing: Share relevant data trends with our broader coalition partners through the VoteGuard platform. 4. VoteGuard Coalition Coverage Coordination VoteGuard is Michigan United’s partner-facing tool used to share volunteer coverage plans and collaborate transparently across the progressive ecosystem. Primary Updates: Populate VoteGuard with Michigan United’s primary election coverage footprint well ahead of the early voting window. General Election Entry: Manage data entry for 200+ target sites in VoteGuard prior to the start of general early voting. Coalition Collaboration: Connect with partner organizations to minimize coverage overlap and maximize the collective footprint across key regions. Strategic Visibility: Stay informed of partner deployments via VoteGuard to help guide Michigan United's own field strategies. 5. BOB Field Data System Administration BOB (Bob the Voter) is Michigan United’s internal data application where field volunteers input real-time qualitative and quantitative updates directly from polling locations. System Administration: Act as the lead administrator for the BOB system within the division. Volunteer Onboarding: Train field volunteers on data entry protocols prior to active deployment windows. Real-Time Monitoring: Keep a pulse on incoming data during early voting and Election Day, flagging anomalies or reporting gaps to the team. Reporting: Convert raw field data into accessible post-election reports and reflection summaries within 30 days of an election. Tech Collaboration: Work closely with the internal technology team to test features, provide feedback, and maintain system health. Long-Term Planning: Ensure field data maps cleanly into our long-term precinct models to assist with future cycle planning. 6. Policy Tracking and Legislative Intelligence To navigate an ever-evolving policy landscape, the Associate tracks legislative shifts to inform our field operations and voter education efforts. Legislative Monitoring: Stay updated on key federal and state voting rights policies, bills, and ballot initiatives. Coalition Tables: Participate regularly in spaces like the PTV Policy and Legislative Meeting and the MI CES Workgroup. Leadership Briefings: Provide monthly written updates on legislative statuses to the Deputy Director during active program cycles. Educational Integration: Share relevant legislative updates with the Voter Services and Access Associate to help keep Know Your Rights curricula up to date. 7. Field Logistics and Cross-Lane Coordination Assignment Matrix: Create comprehensive site assignment schedules detailing volunteer roles, shift times, and supervisor contacts before each election. Safety Coordination: Coordinate closely with the Democracy Defenders program to align volunteer placements at high-priority locations. Program Integration: Align site selections and logistics collaboratively with the Poll Chaplains program. Legal Corps Liaison: Partner with the Election Legal Volunteer Corps to coordinate attorney coverage schedules and legal observer placements. Reporting Rhythms: Share regular progress reports with the Deputy Director during peak preparation and deployment w

Join our multidisciplinary team of policy analysts, economists, attorneys, business analysts, scientists, and engineers. We combine legal, economic, engineering, and scientific research and analysis to solve unique public policy challenges through innovative, accurate, timely, and high-quality products and services. Our dynamic work environment involves working on multiple projects simultaneously, supporting a wide range of clients, and providing a wide range of support services. The position will be REMOTE or have the option to be located in our Reston, Virginia headquarters with hybrid schedule. item.title: Deputy Auditor County Road Districts Elections
item.description: This position is located in Custer, SD. Relocation or commute required. Custer County is currently accepting applications for a full-time Deputy Auditor – Elections & Road Districts. This position is ideal for someone who is detail-oriented, dependable, and ready to support a wide range of county operations, including voter registration, election administration, County Commission support, road district administration, financial tracking, and general office operations. The ideal candidate will be organized, adaptable, and comfortable working both independently and as part of a team. Strong communication skills, excellent customer service, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment are essential. The successful candidate must be able to maintain confidentiality while working with sensitive election, financial, and personnel information. This is a full-time position with a Monday–Friday schedule (8:00 AM – 5:00 PM), starting at $19.04 per hour, with a comprehensive county benefits package, paid leave, and opportunities for professional growth within county government. The position reports to the County Finance Officer. Key responsibilities include: Registering voters, maintaining voter registration records, processing absentee ballots, and assisting with all aspects of county, state, and federal elections. Creating and managing elections within the South Dakota election management system, including candidate setup, ballot preparation, legal notices, and election reporting. Ordering ballots and election supplies, coordinating polling locations, programming and testing voting equipment, and recruiting, hiring, scheduling, and training election workers. Maintaining election records and ensuring compliance with South Dakota election laws and records retention requirements. Providing administrative support to the County Commissioners, including scheduling, meeting preparation, document management, and other administrative duties. Assisting Road Districts with organization, elections, boundary questions, and other administrative matters. Tracking and maintaining county vehicle titles and inventory, coordinating vehicle insurance coverage, and preparing insurance renewal documentation. Providing exceptional customer service by assisting the public, County departments, elected officials, and outside agencies in person, by phone, email, and other forms of communication. Processing mail, maintaining electronic and paper filing systems, ordering office supplies, and preparing official correspondence, reports, and meeting documents. Assisting with school and township fund apportionments, payroll processing, employee benefit administration, and other financial support functions. Assisting the Treasurer's Office with cash counting and financial reconciliation as needed. Maintaining department procedures, job manuals, and administrative records. Attending training opportunities related to elections, county government, records management, and professional development. Performing a variety of office support duties and assisting with special projects and other duties as assigned. Minimum Qualifications: High school diploma or GED required; Associate degree in Business Administration, Accounting, Public Administration, Office Administration, or a related field preferred. One (1) year or more of clerical, administrative, bookkeeping, payroll, customer service, or office support experience preferred. Government, election administration, finance, accounting, or records management experience is a plus. Knowledge of South Dakota election laws, road district administration, or local government operations is beneficial. Strong computer skills, including proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and the ability to learn specialized election and county software systems. Excellent organizational skills with strong attention to detail, accuracy, and recordkeeping. Ability to prioritize multiple assignments while maintaining confidentiality and professionalism. Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to establish positive working relationships with coworkers, elected officials, outside agencies, and the public. Ability to perform the physical requirements of the position, including sitting, standing, walking, lifting up to 25 pounds, and handling election materials and office equipment. This position is primarily performed in a professional office environment with frequent interaction with the public. Occasional evening or weekend work may be required during election cycles to support election preparation and administration. Custer County is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

item.title: Election Day Field Support Fed San Francisco Department Of Elections 1402 Junior Clerk
item.description: Department Background The mission of the Department of Elections (Department) is to provide equitable access to voting and election-related services and to conduct free, fair, and functional elections for the City and County of San Francisco. Department staff work year-round to ensure that every eligible San Franciscan has easy access to safe, barrier-free registration and voting options. The Department also works continuously to improve its elections programs with the goal of making them ever more efficient and responsive to the needs of San Francisco voters. The Department strives to cultivate a workplace environment in which employees of all racial and ethnic backgrounds feel respected, valued, and supported in providing the fairest and most effective services possible to San Francisco residents. The Department is committed to maintaining an inclusive workplace and to providing the training and resources necessary for all employees to succeed in delivering equitable services to city residents. The Department is committed to reaching job seekers of all backgrounds. Everyone, including job seekers from underrepresented communities, is strongly encouraged to apply. Position Description In preparation for the November 3, 2026, General Election, the Department is seeking applications for seasonal positions of roving Field Election Deputies (FEDs) to provide support to Poll Workers at polling places on Election Day. FEDs serve from approximately 5:00 a.m. to approximately midnight, first visiting and confirming polling places are set up and opened on time, then monitoring procedural compliance and ensuring poll workers are carrying out their tasks properly and following health and safety protocols. Finally, FEDs assist with polling place closing procedures as needed. Each FED is responsible for a territory of approximately 7 to 10 polling places and is provided with a van. To prepare for Election Day, FEDs must complete several training sessions. In addition to the above-listed tasks, the person in this position will be responsible for the range of duties assigned to the 1402 job code: 1402-Junior Clerk | City and County of San Francisco . Position Schedule, Requirements , and Work Location This is a temporary exempt as-needed position. Temporary exempt as-needed employees who have worked more than 1040 hours in any consecutive 12-month period, and whose normal work week at the time of inclusion in the system is not less than 20 hours are eligible for health coverage and retirement benefits. For more information on the City and County of San Francisco benefit policies, refer to the Department of Human Resources website at https://careers.sf.gov/benefits/ . This is a short-term assignment (approximately a total of 20-35 hours), that includes completion of mandatory training sessions and performing FED duties on Election Day. Actual start of training date is contingent upon completion of the onboarding process and the Department’s operational needs. There may be additional elections tasks and projects before, during, and after Election Day. This position requires applicants to have: A valid California Driver’s License and a clean DMV record No more than 2 points within the last 3 years, and no more than 1 point in the last year are allowed No DUI’s, reckless driving and endangerment within the last 10 years Regular City driving/ parking experience Experience driving for extended hours (breaks will be provided) Ability to lift a minimum of 25 lbs. Position Salary: $29.55 to $35.9125 hourly $61,464 to $74,698 annually Minimum Qualifications Six (6) months of clerical experience including preparing and maintaining a variety of records and/or documents, filing, use of office equipment, public contact and processing of incoming and outgoing mail. Substitution: Completion of 15 semester units (or equivalent quarter units) of coursework from an accredited college or university; OR Completion of a clerical training program (240 hours); OR Completion of an approved City and County of San Francisco Clerical Administrative training program. Desired Qualifications Ability to track and address numerous high-priority tasks simultaneously with a professional and confident demeanor Diplomatic and conscientious people-management skills Ability to lift up to 50 pounds Ability to use, or learn how to use, a Smart Phone Ability to safely drive and park a large vehicle (minivan or SUV) Commitment to ensuring the following: Voters are offered materials and assistance that allow them to independently cast a secret ballot free from intimidation All election laws are upheld, and procedures are consistently followed. To be considered for this position, applications must be received by 5 p.m., August 7, 2026. Additional Requirement: Applicants must have a valid California driver's license and a clean DMV record. Successful candidates will be required to show their valid CA driver’s license and provide a copy of their latest DMV record before an offer can be made. If you have any questions regarding this recruitment or application process, please contact the Elections Hiring Team at [email protected] . Additional Information Regarding Employment with the City and County of San Francisco: Carol Isen - Human Resources Director All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. The City and County of San Francisco encourages women, minorities and persons with disabilities to apply. Applicants will be considered regardless of their sex, race, age, religion, color, national origin, ancestry, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition (associated with cancer, a history of cancer, or genetic characteristics), HIV/AIDS status, genetic information, marital status, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, military and veteran status, or other protected category under the law.

item.title: Site Selection Manager
item.description: About Fluidstack We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it. We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI. We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply! How We Operate Extreme ownership. Full autonomy. Own things end to end often taking on scope outside your core role without being asked to get things done. Velocity. We drive everything forward as fast as possible. First principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins. Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward. The Development Team Examples of key problems the team is working on Find enough land to deploy multiple gigawatts a week. By 2030 we need to bring on multiple gigawatts of new capacity every week, which means securing sites at a pace and scale no one in the industry has operated at. You'll own finding and locking that land ahead of the build. Get power online in months, not years. Most of the clock runs before the lease is ever signed. You'll optimize the pre-signature work, site diligence, permitting, and development, so a site goes from signed lease to live power in under six months. Acquire 10s to 100s of GWs behind the meter. Reaching that scale means generating on-site instead of waiting on grid interconnection. You'll secure the land and behind-the-meter solar generation to get there. Role Scope Lead the site procurement strategy for the US data center portfolio, sourcing and evaluating powered land for large-scale development and negotiating leases with data center operators. Conduct site due diligence: evaluate utility and behind-the-meter power at 200MW+ scale, and assess buildability through title docs, surveys, geotechnical reports, and environmental studies. Understand permitting requirements at each site and their implications for the construction schedule. Maintain relationships with brokers, landowners, and developers so a valid site is never missed, and run vendor due diligence including on-site audits with specialist engineers. Work directly with DC Design to keep sites matched to the latest technical requirements, and own capacity planning and forecasting across clients and regions. Partner with Finance on multi-year infrastructure investment and cost structures, and lead commercial negotiations with landowners and developers. What We're Looking For The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would . You've worked in real estate with a focus on data centers or other large industrial projects, and you've closed large, complex deals. You assess land viability for data center development fast and rigorously: power, buildability, and permitting. You bring a customer-centric mindset, strong ownership, and proactive problem-solving. You align stakeholders across diverse internal and external teams, and you'll travel 20%+ as projects require. Bonus: Behind-the-meter power evaluation. Hyperscale-scale land deals. Utility interconnection familiarity. Multi-region portfolio planning. Salary & Benefits Competitive total compensation package (salary + equity). Retirement or pension plan, in line with local norms. Health, dental, and vision insurance. Generous PTO policy, in line with local norms. We are committed to pay equity and transparency. Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law. You will receive a confirmation email once your application has successfully been accepted. If there is an error with your submission and you did not receive a confirmation email, please email careers@fluidstack.io with your resume/CV, the role you've applied for, and the date you submitted your application-- someone from our recruiting team will be in touch.

Applicants with previous agricultural or production experience will be considered preferred. Applicants must reside in the United States to be considered for an interview. Requirements: Must have at least 12 months of consecutive work history with one employer and no additional job gaps in employment greater than 6 months in the past 36 months. If applicant has been laid off or providing child or elder care, the employment gap will be increased to 18 months. Previous work history will not apply to applicants who have been full time students consecutively for the last 36 months. Rehire criteria is a minimum waiting period of 180 days. Rehire Rule of no more than 3 times worked at Cobb/Tyson Foods. Company: Cobb Position Summary: This position is responsible for handling birds and equipment for selection process by performing all essential duties in rotation with others. Other duties may be assigned. Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Prepare and setup for selection process by loading coops and equipment into truck/trailer for transport to brothe oding area and unload at the designated house, setup equipment for selection process per instructions (10%) Select birds by performing the following duties: Isolate no more than 200 birds into catch frame for selection as many times as necessary until all birds are selected; catch birds per animal welfare standards; identify gender; verify line by observing wing band color; hold clean wing band under scanner for data entry; place bird in scale cone to obtain weight repeating multiple times until complete; monitor bird groups and “stir” to avoid crowding per animal welfare guidelines; place birds received from selector in designated location such as market pen, breeder candidate coop per gender, full dissect, leg dissect based upon characteristics as instructed by selector. If designated as market remove wing bands and mark head with colored food grade dye prior to placing in area designated for market birds multiple times until complete (60%) Load, transport, and unload coops of birds to feed conversion house and/or dissection lab (10%) Euthanize off condition birds using the cervical dislocation method based upon animal welfare guidelines (10%) Other duties, responsibilities, and activities: Other duties, responsibilities and activities may change or be assigned at any time with or without notice. Such as: Move partitions, back trailer, clean and sanitize equipment for movement between areas per biosecurity requirements, operate a high pressure and regular water hose, maintain equipment by checking fluid levels, filters, tire pressure, and clean/disinfect to remove debris, maintains foot pans and hand sanitizer, maintains a clean and organized work area. (10%) Biosecurity/Animal Welfare Requirements: The jobsite is a biosecure environment which requires showering, changing clothing and footwear before entering the facility. Appropriate clothing and footwear are provided by the Company. No jewelry may be worn on the jobsite except for medical ID jewelry and body piercings covered by appropriate clothing. Must be willing to sign an agreement to avoid any avian species (chickens, ducks, birds, etc.). Must be willing to sign and abide by the Company Biosecurity and Company Animal Welfare Guidelines. Physical Demands and Work Environment: Physical: Must use safe lifting techniques. Must regularly catch, carry, and control individual birds weighing from 3.5 to 12 pounds , lift and move empty coops weighing up to 16 pounds each, buddy lift and carry coops with birds weighing up to 88 pounds , and pull/push stacks of coops with birds weighing up to 360 pounds . While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand majority of shift (concrete floor); walk; sit; use hands to handle, or feel objects, tools, or controls; reach with hands and arms; balance; stoop; talk or hear. Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision; distance vision; color vision; peripheral vision; depth perception; and the ability to adjust focus. Tools and Equipment: Requires use of hand tools such as wire cutters, pliers, wrenches, broom, squeegee, shovel, counter; power tools such as cordless drill; equipment such as catch frames, scales, tables, scanners, extension cords, coops; safe operation of vehicle to and from work area. Environment: Required to work on wet, slippery surfaces and in hot, dry, dusty, wet and cold environments. Personal Protective Equipment Required: safety goggles and/or glasses, chemical gloves, waterproof apron, and rubber boots are required. Must wear company provided facial covering. Ear plugs, arm protectors, and NIOSH approved N95 particulate respirators may be worn as desired. Chemicals Commonly Used: Disinfectants, vehicle fluids, and lubricants. Safety: Team member is expected to follow all applicable safety policies and procedures. These include but are not limited to Hazard Communication, Respiratory Protection, LOTO and Personal Protective Equipment. Team member is expected to identify, address and mitigate safety related risks. Company: Cobb Relocation Assistance Eligible: No Work Shift: 1ST SHIFT (United States of America) Certain roles at Tyson require background checks. If you are offered a position that requires a background check you will be provided additional documentation to complete once an offer has been extended. Hourly Applicants ONLY -You must complete the task after submitting your application to provide additional information to be considered for employment. The successful candidate(s) must be willing and able to perform the physical requirements of the job with or without a reasonable accommodation. Tyson is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will be considered without regard to race, national origin, color, religion, age, genetics, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or veteran status. If you would like to learn more about your data privacy rights and how you may use that information, please read our Job Applicant Privacy Notice here . item.title: Manager Of Government Affairs
item.description: The Cato Institute is seeking applications for a full-time position located in Washington, D.C., to serve as a Manager of Government Affairs. The Manager will work to maintain Cato as a prime source for objective analysis for federal policymakers and to ensure that Cato scholars have access to and the proper tools needed to help Congress and the executive branch develop and advance principled policy solutions. Reporting to Cato’s Director of Government Affairs, the Manager will work closely with the existing federal affairs team and appropriate policy scholars to devise and execute engagement strategies for a portfolio of domestic policy issues. This portfolio will include, but is not limited to, policy areas such as criminal justice reform, civil liberties, civil asset forfeiture, technology, education, and immigration. This is a hybrid position in Washington, DC. The projected salary range for this role is $65,000 - $100,000 per year. Compensation is based on the successful candidate's educational background, experience, and skills. About Cato The Cato Institute is a public policy research organization – a think tank – dedicated to the principles of individual liberty, limited government, free markets, and peace. Its scholars and analysts conduct independent, nonpartisan research on a wide range of policy issues. Founded in 1977, Cato owes its name to Cato’s Letters , a series of essays published in 18th-century England that presented a vision of a society free from excessive government power. Those essays inspired the architects of the American Revolution. And the simple, timeless principles of that revolution – individual liberty, limited government, and free markets – turn out to be even more powerful in today’s world of global markets and unprecedented access to information than Jefferson or Madison could have imagined. Social and economic freedom is not just the best policy for a free people, it is the indispensable framework for the future. The Cato Institute is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Responsibilities Build and maintain relationships with policymakers in Congress and the executive branch Identify, create, and assist with opportunities for Cato scholars to provide congressional testimony, statements for the record, and other high-impact opportunities for Cato scholars Track and advise Cato scholars and staff on ongoing and emerging dynamics in Congress and the executive branch to ensure Cato’s maximum impact on the policy debate Devise, recommend, and execute engagement strategies for the issue portfolio with the goal of positively influencing the policy debate Oversee distribution of Cato scholarship to an audience in Congress and the executive branch Work with existing federal affairs staff to ensure Cato-wide coordination of the Institute’s efforts Exercise exceptional judgment to ensure the protection and enhancement of Cato’s reputation for excellence, integrity, and dedication to principle Education/ Experience A bachelor’s degree in political science, economics, or a related field Three to six years of issue-management experience in Congress or the executive branch, or similar experience with a think tank, association, or in the for-profit sector Demonstrated experience with policy analysis and communicating policy positions to external audiences A demonstrated appreciation for Cato’s mission and principles Comprehensive understanding of congressional rules, procedures, and operations Skills Excellent project management skills with the ability to carry a project from conception to completion Strong oral and written communication skills Innovative, creative thinking with knowledge of creating events of various sizes and target audiences Detail-oriented with strong administration and execution skills Excellent interpersonal skills and an outgoing personality Strong work ethic with an enthusiastic, positive attitude Preferred Qualifications Experience with domestic policy areas with specific emphasis on immigration or legal/judiciary issues To Apply Please submit the following materials: Benefits All Cato employees are provided with: Medical, dental, and vision insurance Employer contribution to a Health Savings Account (HSA) Generous vacation and sick days Paid parental leave Employer-provided life and disability insurance 401(k) employer match Transit/ Parking benefits Pet discount plan Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. This position does not offer visa sponsorship.

item.title: Source Selection Advisor Sme
item.description: Position Summary Hive Group, a HUBZone-certified SDVOSB and multiple award-winning organization, delivers innovative solutions for complex, mission-critical federal programs. We are seeking a highly skilled Source Selection Advisor - Subject Matter Expert to provide senior leader advisory support and strategic oversight for the Missile Defense Agency (MDA) Technical Advisory and Assistance Services (TACS) program located at Redstone Arsenal Huntsville AL. In this high-visibility role, you will act as the principal advisor to Source Selection Evaluation Boards (SSEBs), Advisory Councils (SSACs), and Source Selection Authorities (SSAs) across multiple complex, multi-million-dollar defense acquisitions. You will perform independent, high-level analyses of source selection schedules, documentation, and processes to forecast risk and ensure strict compliance with DoD and MDA Source Selection Procedures. This position is tailored for a seasoned acquisition executive with a background equivalent to a GS-15 or senior military leader. You will shape the future of agency procurement by collaborating with the Enterprise Procurement Innovation Cell (EPIC) to research and deploy cutting-edge contracting solutions. If you hold a Bachelor's degree, a DAWIA Level III certification, and have a proven track record of successfully guiding senior leaders through complex FAR Part 15 source selections and formal contract protests, we invite you to lead this vital enterprise mission. This role requires an Active TS/SCI Personnel are required to be on-site at Redstone Arsenal AL. Key Responsibilities Provide source selection senior leader advisory support, to include independent review of: Source Selection Plans (SSP), solicitations, exchanges with Industry, review of source selection documentation (e.g., Evaluation Notices (ENs), Competitive Range Decision Documents (CRDD), Proposal Analysis Reports (PAR), Source Selection Decision Documents (SSDD), and associated competitive range and decision briefings) and debriefings in accordance with the DoD and MDA Source Selection Procedures, including MDA Instruction 5013.06-INS. Collaborate simultaneously with multiple Source Selection Evaluation Boards (SSEBs), Source Selection Advisory Councils (SSACs), and Source Selection Authorities (SSAs) to identify potential problem areas and advise source selection teams in matters related to the development of solicitations, evaluation of proposals, exchanges with industry, and evaluation documents. Conduct independent senior analysis of source selection schedules, solicitation documentation, processes, or procedures to inform the SSA, SSAC, SSEB, PCO, Source Selection Director, or other cleared personnel, of any associated risks or potential impacts. Assist the Source Selection Directorate in development of source selection templates, dissemination of best practices and lessons learned, and conducting research and outreach on source selection topics and other related topics, as required. Develop and deliver general and procurement-specific source selection training, Directorate Enterprise Procurement Innovation Cell (EPIC) related training, conduct any other required miscellaneous training, and participate in Government teleconferences, meetings, or out-briefs, as required. Assist the EPIC in conducting research, developing proposed courses of action, outreach to other Government entities for collaborative purposes, development of contracting innovation processes and procedures, and dissemination of best practices and lessons learned as required. Qualifications ACTIVE TS/SCI Required. Minimum of a Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, Contract Management or equivalent field. Prior experience as a GS-15, or equivalent positions in the military, a DoD buying activity or civilian agency which executed assisted acquisitions on behalf of DoD activities. Minimum of 10 years of prior experience as a warranted contracting officer or program manager in a DoD buying activity, or civilian agency which executed assisted acquisitions on behalf of DoD activities. DAWIA Level III Certification in Contracting or Program Management. Direct experience in advising and/or conducting/leading more than five (5) source selections, including one or more procurement protests within DoD, or a civilian agency in support of DoD activities/agencies. Experience with FAR Part 15 formal source selection procedures, FAR Subpart 16.505 ordering procedures; and FAR Part 33.1. Demonstrated experience and capability to advise the federal government on all aspects of the acquisition life cycle to implement and adopt innovative acquisition solutions. Compensation and Benefits The estimated compensation range for this position is between $223,700 - $247,300 annually. Actual salary is determined by a variety of factors, including the candidate’s specialized skills, certifications, and years of experience. Hive Group offers a competitive and comprehensive benefits package, including health insurance (medical, dental, vision), life and disability insurance, retirement contributions, paid leave, federal holidays, professional development opportunities, and lifestyle benefits. A Commitment to Equal Opportunity Hive Group is an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer dedicated to fair and unbiased employment decisions. We do not discriminate based on race, color, sex (including gender and transgender status), age, religion, national origin, disability, marital status, veteran status, domestic partner or civil union status, gender identity, medical condition, genetic information, sexual orientation, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, and local laws. Our hiring and promotion decisions are based exclusively on an individual's qualifications and suitability for the role. Protecting Your Information Stay vigilant against fraudulent job offers and individuals impersonating Hive Group Talent Acquisition Specialists. Hive Group will never request payment details or money during the application process. Official communications will only come from email addresses ending in @hive-llc.com or @applytojob.com — not from free email services like Gmail or messaging platforms such as WhatsApp. If you receive suspicious messages requesting payment or personal information, please report them immediately to [email protected] .
